turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's eyes flicked between Sandip and Nikhil, and she wondered what truth lay behind Nikhil's words.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip is a fool to think that the Mussulmans would ever hesitate to attack him, given the provocation he has provided

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: He seemed to be taking Nikhil's words very lightly, but was it just a facade?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was fuming, he muttered, what was all this fuss about the Mussulmans, couldn't Nikhil and Bimala see he was busy with his own affairs?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip is a fool to think that the Mussulmans would ever hesitate to attack him, given the provocation he has provided, and it is not a matter of fear, but of reality

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was dead tired, he told Nikhil and Bimala, and he wouldn't be intimidated by Nikhil's tales of Mussulman wrath. Can't you see he's busy with his own affairs, not some schoolboy's game of hide-and-seek?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: It seemed to her that Nikhil's words were laced with a sense of urgency, one that Sandip seemed to be ignoring.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip rolled his eyes, what a load of hogwash, Nikhil was spouting off again, no doubt to impress Bimala with his bravery

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's words hung in the air, a stern warning to Sandip: This was no laughing matter, the Mussulmans were not to be taken lightly, and he cautioned Sandip once more, not to underestimate their intentions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip sneered at Nikhil, what a master of the obvious, spouting off about the Mussulmans' supposed intentions, as if he, Nikhil, was some sort of seer.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: It seems, Nikhil, that Sandip's words do little to hide his own concerns, even if he chooses to dismiss them as mere fantasy

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's expression turned stern, he said, The Mussulmans' threats must be taken seriously, and he would not stand idly by while Sandip risked the safety of their people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was tired of Nikhil's lectures, he thought, and he wondered what Nikhil's stake was in all this, what made him so brave, hmm?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's bluster is a shield to hide his true nature, and it will be his downfall if he does not take heed of the warnings.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip seems to be underestimating the gravity of the situation, does he not, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip would do well to recall the fate of the zamindars who ignored the whispers of war, their grand estates reduced to ashes and their people scattered to the winds.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ha! Nikhil, always dashing in with his doom-mongering, never a word of optimism, what a perfect zamindar he'd make - a master of gloom.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip's dismissal of Nikhil's warnings may be a sign of his own unease, does Nikhil not think so?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip would do well to remember the lessons of history, lest he wish to suffer the same fate as those who have ignored the warning signs of war.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was incredulous, he thought, playing the prophet now, Nikhil? History's lessons, indeed, and what's the lesson he was trying to impart here?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
